ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary statutes: (1) Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML Law), implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; (2) Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 and the Law of 29 March 2023; (3) Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 August 2019 on the RBE; (4) CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; (5) Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (1915 Company Law), particularly Articles 201-1 to 201-22 on the Special Limited Partnership and Articles 101 et seq. on the registered office; (6) Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and annual accounts (RCS Law); (7) Law of 31 May 1999 on corporate domiciliation.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level_notes: The Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) is publicly searchable via lbr.lu for name, nationality, country of residence, month/year of birth and nature/extent of the beneficial interest; full address, exact date of birth and national identification data are restricted to competent authorities and AML-obliged professionals. The regime is not nominee-friendly; nominee arrangements must be disclosed and do not extinguish UBO identification duties.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_piercing_framework_scsp_note: For the SCSp, the law requires look-through to natural persons behind any corporate general partner and any limited partner holding, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of capital, voting rights or control. Where no UBO can be identified, the general partner or senior managing official is registered as fallback and the LPA must contain a UBO waterfall and identification covenant. Criminal liability attaches to false UBO declarations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable under the origin country regime

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or company registry of the origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable under the origin country regime

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; Article 25-1 et seq. (provisions specific to Sociétés en Commandite Spéciale, introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) acting as the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contrat de Société (Partnership Agreement) duly signed by the general and limited partners and deposited for registration with the RCS; publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; the SCSp may be formed with zero capital. The amount and nature of capital contributions are freely determined in the partnership agreement. No escrow account is required by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: 1. The partnership agreement as tabled is adopted, and the general partner is directed to sign it. 2. The registered office of the SCSp is fixed at the registered address in Luxembourg, to be notified to the Luxembourg Business Registers. 3. [Name] is appointed as manager of the .SCSp with full authority to represent the partnership, enter into bank accounts, and execute legal documents. 4. The manager is instructed to complete all RCS filings, RESA publication, and incidental statutory registrations. 5. These resolutions take effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional) or parties directly; for filing with the RCS, an acknowledged signature is sufficient if private deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Contrat de Société specifying the legal form SCsp, corporate purpose (cloud document automation and e-signature authentication), the identity of general and limited partners, profit-sharing rules, contribution schedule, registered office address, management clause, and transfer rules. Execute the agreement by all partners, with legalisation of signatures if using a private deed. If the partnership acquires immovable property, notarisation is mandatory.
required_dossiers: Contrat de Société (partnership agreement)
Identification documents (passport or national ID) of all general and limited partners
Proof of registered office address (lease or ownership title)
Draft declaration of acceptance of office by the general partner/manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the deed for legal insufficiency or missing information, the partnership agreement is revised, re-signed as necessary, and a fresh filing is submitted within the registry's correction window, usually 15 calendar days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the partnership agreement with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronic portal via www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the LBR e-filing platform using an authenticated identity (Luxtrust, European eID, or Token). Submit the partnership agreement and all attached annexes in electronic format (PDF) together with the structured creation form. Pay any applicable publication fee, if introduced by law. The RCS examines the file for completeness and legal conformity.
required_dossiers: Executed and signed partnership agreement (PDF)
Identification documents of all partners and managers
Registered office address proof
Acceptance of appointment of the manager
Structured filing form (Formulaire de dépôt électronique)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the LBR issues a query or refusal, within 15 days the filer must provide such additional documents or explanations as are requested, amend the deed with the prior consent of the parties, or re-file the corrected deed. Any conflicting legal references are adjusted to comply with RCS requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the formation in the RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Government electronic gazette 'Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations' (RESA) operated by the Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the registry automatically transmits the formation extract to RESA for publication. This publication is mandatory for the SCSp to be opposable to third parties. The manager should however verify the published extract within 2 days to ensure name, registered office, and partner details are accurately reflected.
required_dossiers: Extract of the RCS entry (provided by LBR)
Approval of the publication text by the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published extract contains erroneous data, the manager must immediately file a rectification request with the RCS, accompanied by a corrected schedule, which then republishes the amended extract in RESA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Luxembourg EORI and VAT registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Single point of contact: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Guichet Unique (l'etablissement public for business registration, now part of ITM / Luxembourg Business Registers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the national onboarding form via the Saas platform (Cadastre legalisation via myguichet.lu). Register the SCsp for Luxembourg VAT (standard rate 17%) and EORI number if cross-border physical movement of goods is expected. Since the business sells SaaS services to clients in Luxembourg and abroad, VAT may be due under the B2B reverse-charge rule; however registration is mandatory for local invoicing if annual turnover exceeds EUR 35,000 threshold (or immediately for imports).
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Copy of the partnership agreement
Valid identification of the manager and general partner
Description of business activities with ISIC/NACE code 6201
Bank account details (for refunds, if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT rejects or queries the registration, the applicant corrects the business description, clarifies the legal representation, or submits the missing supporting documents through the same online portal within the specified deadline, usually 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for data protection and electronic trust services
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission Nationale pour la Protection des Données (CNPD) and Ministry of Economy (for e-signature conformity assessment)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the business includes e-signature authentication, an internal data processing register must be kept under GDPR Article 30. Appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO) if the activity entails large-scale systematic monitoring or sensitive data. If the company offers its own digital signature certificates, notify the CNPD of the processing and, where applicable, submit to the national accreditation scheme for 'qualified trust services' under the eIDAS Regulation.
required_dossiers: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) article 30 processing record
Privacy policy and terms of service
DPO appointment (if required)
Description of the e-signature system and cryptographic supply chain
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CNPD requests a prior authorisation or alternative safeguards, the partnership must halt the relevant processing and revise its data protection impact assessment. For e-signature issues, the conformity evaluation procedure before the Ministry of Economy is reopened and the certificate policy is amended.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – the activity is a pure digital service, not an industrial or physically licensed undertaking.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial or commercial operating licence is required for cloud-based legal contract automation and e-signature services under Luxembourg law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no physical installation, no manufacturing, no emissions source. The activity falls under service sector and is not listed in the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater discharge, no VOC emissions, and no hazardous waste generation. Any electronic waste (servers, laptops, hardware) must be disposed of through an authorised waste collector under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable. The registered office is a commercial administrative space. Employees may perform work remotely or in a shared office; the employer must ensure compliance with general safety at work obligations under the Labour Code (Law of 17 June 1994), including periodic health surveillance and first-aid provisions, but no fire safety certification or structural load inspection is required for an entirely administrative office use without public access.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD – Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT – Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority) for VAT; Administration des douanes et accises (ADA – Customs and Excise Administration) for customs. Unified e-gateway: myGuichet.lu; VAT filing portal: eTVA; business registration: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) Foreign entity must first obtain a Luxembourg RCS registration if it establishes a branch or uses the SCSp vehicle, via the LBR electronic portal (notarial deed or private deed filed within one month of formation); (2) upon RCS registration, the ACD automatically assigns the 13-digit national identification number (matricule) for income tax purposes; (3) for VAT, the non-established taxable person must file Form 704 with the AEDT (via eTVA/myGuichet.lu), supplying proof of foreign business identity, EORI number, foreign VAT/TIN certificate and, unless OSS is used, appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative for VAT; (4) the AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number (numéro de TVA LU) without any capital requirement; (5) for the SCSp, RCS filing precedes tax registration in all cases, and the SCSp registers for VAT in its own name when carrying out taxable activities; digital B2C suppliers to EU consumers may alternatively register under the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) without a full Luxembourg VAT ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the SCSp (Société en Commandite Spéciale) is fiscally transparent under Luxembourg law: no entity-level corporate income tax (CIT) or net wealth tax is levied; each partner is taxed directly on their distributive share of income. Territorial scope: non-resident partners are taxable in Luxembourg only on Luxembourg-source items (Luxembourg permanent establishment, Luxembourg real property, and income attributable to Luxembourg sources); PE-attributable foreign profits may benefit from tax treaty relief or the Luxembourg participation exemption. Tax_Exempt_Zone: none — Luxembourg operates no special economic zones; the SCSp remains fully in the general territorial tax net.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (1) Article 165bis LIR election: the SCSp may irrevocably opt for opaque taxation as a resident corporate taxpayer subject to CIT, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; the election binds the entity for five fiscal years and is the functional Luxembourg equivalent of a check-the-box election. (2) Hybrid mismatch alignment: Luxembourg has transposed ATAD 2 (Law of 21 December 2018); where a partner jurisdiction treats the SCSp as opaque or a hybrid entity is used to create double non-taxation, Luxembourg adjusts the transparency classification ex officio. (3) VAT group election (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the VAT Law allows closely linked Luxembourg taxable persons to form a single VAT person. (4) Treaty-based elections: non-resident partners may claim reduced withholding or exemption via Luxembourg certificate forms (e.g., withholding tax exemption under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or tax treaties).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA – taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) governed by the Law of 12 February 1979 (LTVT), as amended, implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC; customs duty and excise administered separately by the ADA.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €35,000 annual taxable turnover (small-trader exemption, Article 57 LTVT) for Luxembourg-established suppliers of goods and services; €10,000 EU-wide annual threshold for distance sales and electronically supplied services B2C (OSS); no threshold applies to non-established foreign suppliers or to B2B cross-border supplies of services — registration is triggered from the first euro of taxable activity in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2G mandate: invoicing to Luxembourg public authorities is mandatorily processed via PEPPOL (PEPPOL BIS 3.0, UBL or CII, EN 16931) from 1 January 2024 for large suppliers and phased in for all suppliers by 31 March 2025; connectivity via certified PEPPOL access points. B2B: no e-invoicing mandate is currently in force; draft Bill 8325 proposes mandatory structured e-invoicing and e-reporting for B2B transactions from 1 January 2026. Luxembourg does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system; no pre-clearance API exists — VAT is accounted for periodically via the eTVA portal, with EC Sales Lists and customs declarations transmitted through the Customs Single Window (GUM).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports: 0% VAT applies where goods are dispatched or transported outside the EU by the seller or on its behalf; the exporter must obtain and retain proof of physical removal from EU customs territory within 90 days of supply. Intra-EU supplies: 0% VAT under Article 41 LTVT for goods/services supplied to VAT-registered customers in another Member State with valid VAT number and EC Sales List reporting. Cross-border services (LegalTech SaaS and e-signature services): under Article 43 LTVT, B2B services supplied to a taxable person established outside Luxembourg are outside Luxembourg's territorial scope and thus effectively taxed at 0% in Luxembourg; B2C electronically supplied services to EU consumers may be taxed under the OSS at the applicable EU destination rate, while exports of services to third-country consumers are zero-rated. Refund route for non-established taxpayers: Directive 2008/9/EC refund procedure via the Luxembourg VAT refund portal.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — electronic IE-507/ASTER export declaration registered with the ADA customs system, bearing the Movement Reference Number (MRN) confirming release for export
Transport document proving EU exit — Bill of Lading, CMR waybill, Air Waybill, or carrier certificate establishing that the goods left EU territory within 90 days of dispatch
Commercial invoice (full Incoterms, exporter and overseas buyer identity, description, value, and explicit export/zero-rating statement)
Proof of payment and inward remittance — bank statement or inward remittance certificate evidencing receipt of the export proceeds from a non-resident counterparty
Customer's non-resident status evidence — foreign VAT registration certificate, EORI confirmation, or written declaration of establishment outside Luxembourg/EU
Incoterms-linked contract documentation — e-contract, purchase order, or signed delivery confirmation evidencing transfer of risk and export intent
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are systematically audited against the customs export record, transport documents, payment flows and customer status evidence. Where substantiation is missing or false, the 0% rate is retrospectively reversed and the VAT is clawed back at 17%, plus statutory delay interest accruing monthly on the arrears. Administrative fines range from 10% up to 50% of the tax evaded depending on good faith, negligence, or deliberate concealment (Articles 60a and 61 LTVT); criminal tax fraud under the Luxembourg General Tax Law can attract imprisonment from 8 days up to 5 years and/or a fine of up to €100,000. The statute of limitations for reassessment and clawback is 5 years from the end of the relevant assessment year, extended to 10 years in cases of fraud or absence of statutory records. Under the VAT collection rules, the partners of the fiscally transparent SCSp may be held jointly and severally liable for VAT debts attributable to the partnership.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), a member of the Eurosystem, together with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). Luxembourg maintains no separate foreign-exchange administration; the BCL sets domestic monetary and payment-system policy, while the CSSF supervises banking AML/CFT compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full currency convertibility for current and capital account transactions. As a Eurozone member, Luxembourg applies Article 63 TFEU on free movement of capital; there are no exchange controls, no approval requirements for inward or outward transfers, and no restrictions on non-resident ownership of an SCSp. The SCSp is fiscally transparent, is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income, municipal business, or net wealth tax at entity level, and profit distributions to non-resident partners do not attract Luxembourg withholding tax absent substance deficiencies or anti-abuse findings; currency conversion and remittance are therefore unrestricted from an FX-policy standpoint.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export-proceeds surrender or conversion regime exists in Luxembourg. There is no statutory repatriation timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to convert export receipts into EUR. Export and SaaS-subscription proceeds may be retained in any currency in any bank account, subject only to standard CRS/FATCA reporting, Luxembourg income-tax declarations by the partners, and BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting performed by resident banks.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency EUR/USD); Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (multi-currency); Trade Finance and Documentary Credit desk

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; FX and derivatives margin line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium for operational collections and vendor disbursements; Low for capital escrow and surplus liquidity. EU/EEA PSD2-licensed EMIs (Wise, Revolut Business, Airwallex, Mangopay) can onboard the SCSp remotely in most cases, but e-money balances do not benefit from Luxembourg deposit-guarantee protection, and EMI KYC processes frequently reject or delay transparent partnership structures pending LP-agreement and UBO verification. Committed investor capital must flow exclusively through a CSSF-regulated credit institution; EMIs should be limited to rapid Stripe payout sweeps and low-value operating payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement for physical presence exists under the Luxembourg AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004, as amended, or CSSF Regulation 12-02; onboarding follows a risk-based approach. Because the SCSp lacks legal personality, most banks require at least one in-person interview with the General Partner's signatories or the appointed Luxembourg corporate-services agent during opening. Fully remote video identification (eIDAS-compliant qualified electronic signatures) is accepted only by selected banks and generally only for simple, low-risk structures; the practical route is one physical visit to Luxembourg by the GP principal or engagement of a Luxembourg fiduciary domiciliation agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transparent legal form: an SCSp has no legal personality, complicating client identification and control-chain review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS registration excerpt; notarised or dated partnership agreement (contrat de société); certified extract from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) listing UBOs; organisational chart identifying the General Partner chain; certified passports of all signatories and of every partner holding more than 25% or exercising control; signed mandate to a Luxembourg corporate-services agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or high-risk-jurisdiction partners contributing committed capital without audited operational history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations with supporting bank statements; executed subscription agreements; corporate excerpts and tax-residence certificates or CRS self-certifications of corporate limited partners; commercial plan and signed pipeline for the LegalTech SaaS and e-signature platform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic-substance scrutiny: risk of classification as a letterbox or manager-less partnership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg registered office and fiduciary/corporate-services agreement; local bookkeeping and accounting mandate; domiciliation and management-service invoices; board and partner meeting minutes; signed SaaS and contract-automation client contracts; management financial projections evidencing real IT activity and substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlicensed payment-activity suspicion: recurring Stripe and credit-card settlement volumes could be mischaracterised as payment intermediation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SaaS subscription and e-signature authentication agreements demonstrating that the SCSp acts as merchant-of-record for its own software platform; Stripe merchant verification and KYB/KYC documentation; platform and PCI-DSS compliance description; flow diagram showing Stripe settlement directly to the SCSp's operational IBAN with no third-party pass-through obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: CRS/FATCA and tax-transparency risk: US or high-tax-resident partners and potential permanent-establishment exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg tax-opinion memorandum confirming partnership pass-through and absence of Luxembourg withholding; FATCA/CRS self-certification forms and IRS Forms W-8/W-9 of all partners; RBE beneficial-ownership filings; annual substance documentation; transfer-pricing and permanent-establishment analysis memo covering any foreign delivery activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital subscriptions are credited to the SCSp's dedicated capital-contribution account at the Luxembourg bank via SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR or SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR. Remittance information must state the exact SCSp legal name and the partnership agreement execution date. The receiving bank will classify the transfer under the BCL/Eurosystem balance-of-payments framework as cross-border direct-investment equity capital; the SCSp should pre-file the partnership agreement, contribution schedule, and RBE certificate. First-time or high-value wires trigger enhanced due diligence and sanctions screening, but no prior foreign-exchange or central-bank approval is required; source-of-funds evidence and a payment-purpose memorandum must be immediately available. Split transfers to avoid screening thresholds are prohibited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR vendor payments and Stripe settlement sweeps are executed via SEPA Credit Transfer, using T2/TIPS priority rails where same-day value is required; non-EEA counterparties are paid via SWIFT MT103 through the relationship bank's international platform. For procurement of significant IT, legal, or cloud infrastructure from non-EEA suppliers, a commercial letter of credit (UCP600) or documentary collection issued by Société Générale Luxembourg or BGL BNP Paribas provides settlement certainty, with bank confirmation available where vendor credit risk requires it. Stripe settles card receivables in EUR through its EU partner credit institution to the SCSp's operational IBAN; direct merchant acquiring through BGL BNP Paribas or Société Générale acquiring desks keeps consolidated treasury liquidity inside the Luxembourg banking perimeter.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forward under the bank's commercial master agreement or ISDA/CSA documentation
EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF FX forwards to hedge non-EUR client subscription receipts
Non-deliverable FX forwards (NDFs) for restricted or offshore currencies (USD/CNH, USD/INR, USD/BRL) where physical delivery is unavailable
FX swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) for rebalancing multi-currency liquidity beyond twelve months
Vanilla FX options (long call/put) providing asymmetric EUR/USD protection, subject to bank credit lines and EMIR reporting/trade-repository obligations
Same-day interbank spot EUR conversion at T+2 value date via the primary bank's electronic FX trading platform, reducing conversion spread on periodic USD Stripe sweeps

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) of the SCSp prepared by the general partner and provided to the limited partners; no public filing at the RCS applies to an SCSp without legal personality
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General partner and limited partners; accounts retained at the Luxembourg registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end for preparation and partner communication; no statutory deposit deadline at the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: General partner civil liability to partners; accounting-law fines under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 for defective books and records

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO declaration on the Luxembourg Register of Effective Beneficial Owners (RBE) for the SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing within 1 month of RCS registration; update within 1 month of any transfer of partnership interests or change in beneficial ownership; no recurring annual re-filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of EUR 125-250 for late or omitted filing; EUR 250-500 for knowingly false declarations; criminal sanctions for deliberate concealment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RCS corporate event filings (change of general partner or manager, registered office transfer, amendments to the limited partnership agreement, capital or contribution movements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month from the date of each triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 25,000; unregistered acts not opposable to third parties; persistent non-compliance may lead to judicial strike-off (radiation d'office)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Luxembourg direct tax informational return of the fiscally transparent SCSp, reporting allocable income to the general and limited partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year returns due by 31 May of the following year; electronic extension normally granted to 31 December; non-calendar year ends use the six-month post-year-end rule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing coercive fine (Zwangsgeld) up to EUR 25,000 plus 0.6% monthly late-payment interest; tax assessed by estimation and taxable at partner level

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Luxembourg VAT returns covering B2B SaaS and e-signature services (reverse charge on EU business customers; place-of-supply rules for non-EU clients)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly return by the 15th of the following month when annual VAT payable exceeds EUR 15,000; quarterly option below that threshold; annual return below EUR 3,000; annual recapitulative statement by 31 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of VAT due plus 0.6% monthly interest; administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 for repeat violations

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SCSp must appoint an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) when it exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average headcount 50 employees. Mandatory audit also applies if imposed by the limited partnership agreement or if the SCSp is a regulated AIF/Part II fund (CSSF requirement); otherwise the audit remains optional.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 (Plan Comptable Normalisé 2019) is the default statutory framework; IFRS as adopted by the European Union is optional for statutory accounts and available for partner reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg does not impose an annual UBO re-certification. The SCSp files the RBE declaration at formation and updates it within one month of any transfer of limited partnership interests, change in the general partner, or change in control; the general partner nevertheless performs an annual reconciliation of the RBE declaration against the internal register of partners as audit best practice, with EUR 125-250 fines applying to stale or omitted updates.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members - maintained at the qualified registered office as the register of limited partners and archived transfers; the SCSp keeps limited partner identities confidential from the RCS public file
Register of Directors - files recording the appointment, resignation, and powers of the general partner (associé gérant) and any alternate managers
Minute Book - bound records of partner written resolutions, limited partnership agreement amendments, and manager consents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $2,200 - $5,500 per year (EUR 2,000 - 5,000) for a qualified Luxembourg domiciliation agent including corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,500 - $11,000 per year (EUR 3,000 - 10,000) for a low-risk SCSp with a simple SaaS balance sheet; materially higher if CSSF-regulated or consolidated

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at SCSp level due to fiscal transparency; for qualifying corporate partners the aggregate Luxembourg CIT rate is 24.94% (17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax for Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent and is not itself subject to CIT. Corporate partners may benefit from the Luxembourg participation exemption (100% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains where the 10% or EUR 6,000,000 participation threshold and 12-month holding requirement are satisfied) and the IP Box regime (80% exemption of qualifying net IP income, yielding an effective CIT rate of approximately 4.99%). Loss carryforward at partner level is subject to Luxembourg NOL carryforward rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 470 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed through MyGuichet.lu / e-DI electronic portal; for a tax-transparent SCSp, the partnership itself does not file a CIT return, but each partner reports its allocable share on its own Form 470 or equivalent individual/non-resident return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The tax return must be filed by 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end, unless the Luxembourg tax administration grants a formal extension. Taxable partners must report their SCSp-derived income in the tax year in which the SCSp's fiscal year closes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS number, Luxembourg tax identification number, registered office address, and contact details of the tax representative where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate or individual partners must state their overseas address, foreign tax identification number, and the Luxembourg tax representative's address when a trade/business is carried on in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The partner's proportionate share of SCSp profits or losses, adjusted for tax-specific disallowances, depreciation, and deductible charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners include only Luxembourg-source income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment or fixed base, in accordance with Article 104bis of the LIR and applicable DTA provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Adjustments, Transfer Pricing, and Tax Incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Arm's-length transfer pricing corrections, IP Box deduction claims, participation exemption computations, and any anti-abuse adjustments under Article 6 of the Luxembourg Tax Adaptation Law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident claimants must attach transfer pricing documentation, treaty residence certificates, and detailed supporting schedules showing entitlement to reduced withholding tax, treaty relief, or IP Box benefits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers administrative penalties under the Luxembourg General Tax Law, default interest at 0.6% per month on unpaid taxes, and potential ex officio assessment by the Administration des contributions directes. Intentional failure or fraudulent filings can lead to criminal fines of up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment, in addition to civil restitution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by Luxembourg resident companies; distributions made by a transparent SCSp to its partners are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax at the partnership level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the recipient must provide a valid certificate of tax residence (TRC) issued by the competent foreign tax authority, together with a signed declaration of beneficial ownership. For EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, the corporate recipient must hold at least 10% of the SCSp/underlying capital for an uninterrupted 12-month period. The Luxembourg paying agent must receive the TRC and supporting forms before making the distribution; where tax was over-withheld, a refund claim must be filed with the Luxembourg tax administration within the statutory limitation period, generally five years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg generally imposes no withholding tax on cross-border royalties or interest paid by a Luxembourg entity to non-residents. However, interest and royalty payments that are recharacterised as hidden profit distributions become subject to the 15% statutory dividend withholding tax, with treaty reduction available upon proper DTA relief application.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory transfer pricing documentation is required where related-party transactions exceed EUR 50,000 per transaction or EUR 150,000 in aggregate per fiscal year; the documentation must include contemporaneous Local File and Master File consistent with OECD TP guidelines.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the SCSp must demonstrate real economic substance through adequate office space, staff, decision-making, and accounting records. Substance deficiencies can trigger the Luxembourg GAAR, denial of tax residence certificates, and anti-abuse recharacterisation under Article 6 of the Luxembourg Tax Adaptation Law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of SCSp taxable income, falsification of partnership accounts, or abusive use of a transparent SCSp to conceal the true beneficiary of profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative reassessment with default interest at 0.6% per month; penalties ranging from 10% to 100% of underpaid tax; criminal prosecution with fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly sign false declarations or participate in a fraudulent tax scheme face joint and several civil liability, asset seizure, travel bans, and criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length invoicing of contract automation and e-signature services to related foreign entities, excessive royalty payments, or circular transaction arrangements designed to shift Luxembourg profits abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Compulsory transfer pricing adjustment, recalculated taxable base, late-payment interest, and penalties for incorrect tax returns; intentional manipulation is treated as tax fraud and carries criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for additional tax assessments if they certified false transfer pricing reports; directors may be prohibited from managing Luxembourg companies and may face confiscation or travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal SCSp with no office, no employees, no bank account, no accounting records, and no decision-making functions, while routing e-signature and legal contract income through Luxembourg to avoid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification of the SCSp as a tax resident of another jurisdiction, denial of treaty benefits, application of GAAR to reattribute income to the underlying shareholders, mandatory deregistration, and administrative fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil-piercing applies where the SCSp is a sham; directors and shareholders are jointly liable for the entity's tax liabilities and may face criminal charges for abuse of law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using LegalTech SaaS payment rails (Stripe, credit card) to launder proceeds, accepting payments from sanctioned entities without screening, or failing to register and report under Luxembourg AML legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under the amended Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004, including administrative fines up to EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover; criminal sanctions of up to five years' imprisonment and confiscation of illicit funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners face personal monetary fines, director disqualification, travel bans, and imprisonment for willful AML failures; intentional breaches may result in unlimited liability.
